The area is 6√3 + 9π/2 ≈ 24.53, which matches none of the three answers, so I reject all of them. I checked it with polar coordinates centered at O.

**Setup.** Use the coordinates from Solutions 1 and 3, shifted so that O is the origin: S′(3,√3), A′(5,√3), T′(6,2√3), U′(5,3√3), R′(3,3√3), N′(2,2√3). The distances from O and polar angles of the vertices are:

| Vertex | Distance from O | Polar angle |
|---|---|---|
| S | 2√3 ≈ 3.46 | 30° |
| A | √28 ≈ 5.29 | ≈19.1° |
| T | 4√3 ≈ 6.93 | 30° |
| U | √52 ≈ 7.21 | ≈46.1° |
| R | 6 | 60° |
| N | 4 | 60° |

**Closest and farthest points.** The edge SN is perpendicular to OS, so S is the nearest point of the hexagon to O, at distance 2√3. The farthest point is T, at distance 4√3. Edge NR lies along the ray at 60° from O.

**Polar slices.** For each radius r between 2√3 and 4√3, the circle of radius r meets the convex hexagon in a single arc [a(r), b(r)]. I checked this for each range of r using the edge structure above. Rotating through 45° sweeps that arc to [a(r), b(r) + π/4], so the swept length at radius r is (b − a) + π/4.

**Area.**

Area = ∫ r(b − a + π/4) dr = (area of hexagon) + (π/4)·½(r_max² − r_min²).

The hexagon has area 6√3. With r_max² = 48 and r_min² = 12:

(π/4)·½·(48 − 12) = 9π/2.

So the swept area is 6√3 + 9π/2 ≈ 10.392 + 14.137 = 24.53.

**Checks against the solutions.**
- Solution 1 gives 24, with no real derivation. Wrong.
- Solution 2 gives 6√3 + 5π ≈ 26.10. Its boundary-integral value of 20 is wrong; the correct value is 18, giving 9π/2. Wrong.
- Solution 3 gives 16 + 8√3 ≈ 29.86, with no derivation. Wrong.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
